prerequisites: The sets of natural, integer, rational, real numbers and their main properties
Equations of lines and conics as geometric loci

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic concepts of the theory of limits and differential and integral calculus in a real variable.
Know the main properties of the field of complex numbers.
Understand the approximation of functions of a real variable by the use of appropriate polynomials.
Analyze the graph of a function of a real variable.
Analyze mathematical problems that can be approached with differential and integral calculus tools.
Develop a mentality oriented toward problem solving.
Through classroom lessons, learn the main methods of mathematical modeling based on the tools of mathematical analysis.
Through practical exercises, apply the acquired knowledge to solve problems that require typical tools of mathematical analysis.
Independently use the acquired methodological tools useful for continuing their studies and updating their knowledge and skills.
Develop the ability to independently choose the methods of analysis and solution of problems relating to the course program.
Develop the ability to clearly explain the topics covered in the course.

syllabus_topics: Upper extreme and lower extreme. Axiom of completeness.
Sequences. Calculus of limits. The number of Nepero. Infinitesimal and infinite sequences.

Bounded, symmetric, monotone, periodic functions. Limit and continuity. Discontinuous functions. Asymptotes. Composite and invertible functions. Theorem of zeros, of Weierstrass and theorem of intermediate values. Limits of extra interest. Infinite and infinitesimal functions.

Derivative and tangent. Angular points, cusps and flexes with vertical tangent. Continuity and differentiability. Rules of derivation and fundamental derivatives. Stationary points and local extremes. Primitives. Monotonicity test. Search of local and global minima and maxima. De L'Hospital rule. Second derivatives, concavity and convexity. Flexes.
The Reimann integral. Fundamental theorem of integral calculus. Integration by parts and substitution. Improper integrals.
Convergent, divergent and irregular number series. Geometric and harmonic series.
Taylor-MacLaurin formula with the rest according to Peano and according to Lagrange. Taylor series.
Complex numbers in algebraic, trigonometric, and exponential form. Gauss plane. Operations with complex numbers.
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral test. Students can access the oral exam only after passing the written exam, which remains valid throughout the exam session. The grade is the arithmetic average of the evaluations of the two tests. Alternatively, first-year students can pass two partial written tests, with the second test requiring a score of at least 18/30 on the first. The final grade for partial tests is the arithmetic average of both if both are sufficient.
